mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen 22 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w, indicating sustained recovery momentum. This trend will continue over the next four weeks as the baseline effect of reopening persists, driving further retail-and-recreation mobility gains.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -55.4 to -33.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has recovered 14.2 points from t-3w to t-0w, signaling restored commuting confidence. When transit recovery exceeds 10 percentage points over four weeks, retail footfall follows within one week as workers resume shopping during commute windows.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 10 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a TRANSIT recovery of >10 points in at least 70% of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains severely depressed at -25.0 in t-0w, indicating persistent remote work. Retail-and-recreation mobility will remain suppressed because workplace-anchored shopping trips are eliminated, offsetting any ambient recovery.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below -20 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has recovered sharply to -6.4 in t-0w while RETAIL_REC remains at -33.4, indicating essential-shopping prioritization. As grocery confidence stabilizes, discretionary retail will capture the same mobility pool within two weeks, driving RETAIL_REC gains.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -10 percentage points while RETAIL_REC remains below -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 10 percentage points within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM stabilizing above -10 while RETAIL_REC is below -30.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed to -23.6 in t-0w from -25.7 in t-3w, showing volatile outdoor-activity demand. When parks mobility falls below -25 percentage points, consumers redirect leisure time to indoor retail venues, increasing RETAIL_REC within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a PARKS drop below -25 in at least 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 20.1 to 12.9 percentage points above baseline, indicating reduced home confinement. This deconfinement, combined with TRANSIT recovery of 14.2 points, creates a two-factor reopening signal that will drive retail recovery over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below 15 percentage points AND TRANSIT rises above -45 percentage points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean when both RESIDENTIAL is below 15 and TRANSIT is above -45.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has recovered 22 points over four weeks while WORKPLACES remains depressed, indicating a shift toward non-work-anchored retail (weekend, evening, leisure shopping). This behavioral reallocation will sustain over the next four weeks as the new pattern becomes entrenched.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC improves >15 points while WORKPLACES remains below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not maintain or exceed the prior 28-day mean when RETAIL_REC has improved >15 points and WORKPLACES remains below -20.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains severely depressed at -44.7 in t-0w, constraining commute-based retail access. If TRANSIT does not recover above -40 percentage points within two weeks, RETAIL_REC will stagnate or decline because the mobility infrastructure for retail trips remains unavailable.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next two weeks while TRANSIT remains below -40 for two consecutive weeks.
